First listed 2025-07-28 · episode or wrap

How a Short Seller Succeeds: The Blueprint for Strategy and Survival

Eisman and Brad Safalow examine short-selling risk through Freshpet, Trupanion and Kinsale. Eisman discloses a Trupanion short, endorses its apparent deterioration and insists on catalysts and surviving countertrend rallies. Most detailed allegations and forecasts belong to Safalow. Later results support slower Freshpet growth and Kinsale premium pressure but contradict the predicted Kinsale underwriting deterioration and weaken Trupanion’s collapse narrative. The interview is strongest on trade-path risk and the difference between fundamental conviction and realized returns.

How he reasons here

  • Separate company deterioration from profitable trade execution.
  • Demand a catalyst rather than shorting solely on valuation.
  • Inspect insurance cohorts, state filings and policy exclusions.
  • Account for flows and positioning but do not assume they identify every price cause.
